Het paneel Kleur waarschuwt ook voor zulke kleuren. Zonder geladen profielen zet TraceDraw kleuren om met een eigen model van proceskleuren op gestreken papier.

Speciale effecten Effecten veranderen hoe een object eruitziet zonder het object zelf te veranderen: een overvloeiing vult de ruimte tussen twee objecten, een contour tekent ringen om een object, een envelop buigt het, een extrusie laat het massief lijken, een schaduw tilt het van de pagina. De meeste effecten zijn dynamisch: het object houdt zijn eigen vorm, en het effect wordt ervan afgeleid, zodat u het effect altijd kunt wijzigen of verwijderen. De effecten staan in het menu Effecten, in het uitklapmenu Effecten van de gereedschapskist en in eigen panelen. Bitmapeffecten veranderen de pixels van afbeeldingen, of van objecten die als afbeelding worden getekend.

h: Managing effects Other effect commands
x: The Effects panel An object can carry several live effects at once, applied one after the other. The Effects panel lists the effects of the selected object in the order they apply, from the top down. Open it with Window > Panels > Effects.  Managing effects Each row of the list has: a check box that turns the effect on or off. An effect turned off keeps its place and settings, but is not drawn, exported or printed; the effect's name, dimmed while it is off; up and down arrows that move the effect earlier or later, which changes the result (for example a contour of an envelope, or an envelope of a contour); a cross that removes the effect. Every change is one undo step. Each effect is still edited with its own tool or panel. Other effect commands Effects > Flatten Effects turns the effects of the selected objects into plain objects. Effect Picker shows a list of effects to apply to the selection. Object > Clear Effect removes the effect of the selection. Object > Copy Effect copies an effect from another object, and Clone Effect makes a clone that follows it; see Copying and cloning effects.

h: To blend two objects Blend settings Blending along a path Removing or splitting a blend
x: Blends A blend draws a series of intermediate steps between two objects, changing shape, size and color from one to the other. Use it for smooth shading, repeated patterns or a shape that turns into another. To blend two objects With the tool: Choose the Blend tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from the start object to the end object. With the panel: Select two objects. Open the Blend panel with Effects > Blend (Ctrl+F8). Set the options and click Apply.  Both objects stay objects of the drawing: move, resize or recolor either one and the steps follow. Deleting the end object removes the blend. Blend settings With a blend selected, every change on the property bar or in the panel applies at once. Blend steps: the number of steps (5 at first, up to 999). Spacing, for a blend on a path: the distance between steps; the number of steps follows from the length of the path. Rotation: turns the steps progressively; Loop turns them about the middle between the two objects instead. Acceleration: the object slider makes the steps crowd towards one end; the color slider does the same for the colors. Apply to sizing makes the object acceleration change the sizes too, and Link acceleration keeps the two sliders together. Reset puts both back to even. Color Blend: Direct (straight from one color to the other), Clockwise or Counterclockwise (around the color wheel). The tool's property bar has the steps, rotation and the two accelerations. Blending along a path Select the blend. Click New path in the Blend panel and click a curve. The steps follow the curve. Rotate all objects turns each step along the curve, and Blend along full path places the first and last steps at the ends of the curve. Removing or splitting a blend Clear blend removes the steps and leaves both objects. Break apart turns the steps into objects of their own.

h: To add a contour Contour settings
x: Contours A contour draws evenly spaced copies of an object's outline inside it, outside it, or to its center, like the lines of a map. It is a live effect: change the object and the contour follows. To add a contour With the tool: Choose the Contour tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object: away from its middle for an outside contour, towards it for an inside one. The further you drag, the larger the spacing. With the panel: Select an object. Open the Contour panel with Effects > Contour (Ctrl+F9). Set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot take a contour. Contour settings The property bar and the panel show the settings of the selected contour and change it at once. To center, Inside or Outside (at first). Steps: 3 at first, up to 999. To center makes as many as fit. Offset: the distance between steps (2 mm at first). Corners: mitered (sharp, at first), round or beveled. Color direction: direct, clockwise or counterclockwise around the color wheel, from the object's colors to the last step's. The fill and outline colors of the last step (white and black at first). An object without a fill gives unfilled steps. Object acceleration and color acceleration (-100 to 100%) crowd the steps or the colors towards the object or towards the last step. Outside steps are drawn behind the object, inside steps in front of it. Clear contour removes the contour; Break apart turns the steps into objects.

h: To distort an object Distortion settings
x: Distortion The Distort tool bends an object's outline in three ways: push and pull (spikes or petals), zipper (zigzag teeth) and twister (a swirl). It is a live effect: you can change, move or remove the distortion at any time, and the object keeps its own outline. To distort an object Choose the Distort tool from the Effects flyout. Choose the kind on the property bar. Drag on the object. The distortion is centered where you start. Push and pull: drag right to push the nodes out (spiky shapes with hollow sides), left to pull them in (rounded petals). Zipper: the further you drag, the taller the teeth. Twister: drag around the starting point; full turns count. The center of a selected distortion shows as a diamond: drag it to move the center. Dragging again replaces the distortion; an object has at most one. Groups and bitmaps are not distorted. Distortion settings The property bar shows and changes the selected distortion: the kind: Push and pull, Zipper or Twister (choosing another kind changes a selected distortion); for push and pull, the amplitude (-200 to 200, 20 at first); for zipper, the amplitude (0 to 100 mm, 2 mm at first) and the frequency (teeth per segment, 6 at first), with Random (uneven teeth), Smooth (rounded teeth) and Local (teeth shrink away from the center); for twister, clockwise or counterclockwise, the number of whole rotations and the extra degrees. Object > Clear Effect removes the distortion.

h: To add an envelope Editing the frame Envelope settings
x: Envelopes An envelope is a frame of nodes around an object; the object is bent to fill the frame, and follows when you move its nodes. Use it to arch text, bulge a shape or fit artwork into a flag or a circle. The object keeps its own shape, so the envelope can be changed or removed at any time. To add an envelope With the tool: Choose the Envelope tool from the Effects flyout. Click an object. It gets a frame of eight nodes: the corners and the middle of each side. Drag the nodes to reshape the frame. With the panel (Effects > Envelope, Ctrl+F7): Select an object. Click Add new, or click one of the 24 preset shapes (arch, circle, flag, heart, cloud, speech bubble and more) to use it as the envelope.  Editing the frame The editing mode, chosen on the property bar or in the panel, decides what happens to the sides when you drag a node: Straight line: the sides stay straight; Single arc: the sides become one smooth arc; Double arc: the sides become S curves; Unconstrained (at first): the node carries its handles; click a node to see its two handles and drag them to bend each side on its own. Double-click the frame to add a node, a node (other than a corner) to delete it. In the unconstrained mode the property bar also has Add node and Delete node. The Shape tool edits the frame the same way. Envelope settings Presets on the property bar: arch, bulge, squeeze, flag, perspective and circle. Mapping, how the object fills the frame: Putty (at first), Original (spread evenly along the frame), Horizontal or Vertical (only across or only up). Keep lines: straight segments of the object stay straight. Add new envelope puts a fresh frame around the object as it now looks, over the envelope it has. Copy envelope properties: click another object to copy its envelope (as Object > Copy Effect > Envelope From). Clear envelope removes the last envelope.

h: To extrude an object Extrusion settings
x: Extrusions An extrusion turns a flat object into a solid-looking body, with sides that run from its outline to a copy of it, lit and shaded. It is a live effect: change the object and the body follows. To extrude an object With the tool: Choose the Extrude tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object. For a parallel extrusion the body runs along the drag; for the others the end of the drag is the vanishing point. Drag the handle (a square with a cross) to move the vanishing point. With the panel (Effects > Extrude, Ctrl+F10): select an object, set the options and click Apply.  Groups and bitmaps cannot be extruded. Extrusion settings The panel has five pages, chosen with the buttons at its top; the property bar has the main settings and a 3D menu with the rest. Camera: the type of extrusion: small back (at first), big back, small front, big front, back parallel or front parallel. Back types grow behind the object, front types in front of it. The depth (1 to 99, 20 at first), the vanishing point (X and Y, counted from the page origin or the object's center), and whether it is locked to the object (moves with it) or to the page. For parallel types, X and Y are the offset. Rotation: turns the body in space about X, Y and Z (-360 to 360 degrees); Reset puts it back. Lighting: the angle (135 degrees at first), intensity (50 at first) and elevation of the light, and two more lights you can turn on. Color: Object fill (the object's color, at first), Solid (one color) or Shade (a gradient from one color to another on each side). Bevel: a beveled edge on the front face, with its width. Clear extrude removes the extrusion; Break apart turns the faces into objects.

h: To add a block shadow Settings
x: Block shadows A block shadow is a solid shadow that runs straight out from an object, as if the object were a thick block. It is drawn below the object as one filled shape, which suits signs and cut vinyl. To add a block shadow Choose the Block Shadow tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object in the direction the shadow should go. Settings On the property bar: Depth: how far the shadow reaches. Direction: its angle, 0 being to the right, counterclockwise. Color: 60% black at first. Gap: a clear band between the object and the shadow (0 at first). Clear block shadow removes the effect. With a shadowed object selected, the fields change its shadow; otherwise they set the next one.

h: To add a drop shadow Settings
x: Drop shadows A drop shadow is a soft shadow beneath an object, as if it floated above the page. It is a copy of the object's silhouette in the shadow color, offset and blurred. To add a drop shadow Choose the Drop Shadow tool from the Effects flyout. Drag from an object to where the shadow should fall. Settings On the property bar: the offset of the shadow (2 mm right and 2 mm down at first); its opacity (50% at first); its feathering, how soft its edge is (15% at first); its color (black at first). Object > Clear Effect removes the shadow. To copy the shadow of another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Drop Shadow From.

h: Een object een schuine rand geven
x: Schuine randen Een schuine rand laat de randen van een object verhoogd of uitgesneden lijken, door één kant van de rand te belichten en de andere te beschaduwen. Het is een live-effect, ingesteld in het paneel Schuine rand; open het met Effecten > Schuine rand.  Een object een schuine rand geven Selecteer een gevuld object. Kies in het paneel Schuine rand de stijl: Zachte rand: de rand loopt schuin het object in, aan één kant belicht en aan de andere beschaduwd; Reliëf: het object lijkt uit de pagina gedrukt. Stel de Afstand in (hoe ver de schuine rand het object in reikt), de Lichthoek, de Intensiteit van het licht, de Schaduwkleur en de Lichtkleur. Klik op Toepassen. Om een schuine rand van een ander object te kopiëren, gebruikt u Object > Effect kopiëren > Schuine rand van. Object > Effect wissen verwijdert haar. Het paneel voor extrusies heeft ook een schuine rand voor het voorvlak; zie Extrusies.

h: To make a lens Kinds of lens Options
x: Lenses A lens changes how the objects beneath it look, without changing them: it can brighten, tint, magnify, invert or apply bitmap effects to everything it covers. Move the lens and the view through it changes. Lenses are set in the Lens panel (Effects > Lens, Alt+F3).  To make a lens Draw a closed object over the objects to change, and select it. In the Lens panel, choose the kind of lens and its settings. Click Apply. Kinds of lens Brighten brightens (or darkens) what lies beneath rate, -100 to 100 (50) Color add adds a color, as light color and rate Color limit lets only a color through color and rate Custom color map maps dark to light onto a range of colors from and to colors, direction Fish eye bulges what lies beneath rate, -1000 to 1000 (100) Heat map shows brightness as warm and cold colors palette rotation Invert inverts the colors  Magnify enlarges what lies beneath amount, 1 to 100 (2) Tinted grayscale shows it in shades of one color color Transparency makes the lens see-through, tinted rate and color Wireframe shows the objects as outlines outline and fill colors Bitmap effects runs bitmap effects over what lies beneath Add effect, in order Options Frozen: keeps what the lens shows now, even when the objects beneath change. Viewpoint: shows another place through the lens. Remove face: shows the lens only over other objects, not over the empty page. To add a bitmap effect as a lens from the effect picker, choose Effects > Effect Picker and apply it as a lens.

h: Adding perspective to an object Drawing in perspective
x: Perspective Perspective makes an object look as if it lay on a plane that recedes into the distance. You can add perspective to an object you have drawn, or draw straight onto a perspective grid. Adding perspective to an object Select an object. Choose Object > Add Perspective. Drag the four corner nodes with the Shape tool to tilt it. To copy the perspective of another object, use Object > Copy Effect > Perspective From. Drawing in perspective View > Draw in Perspective shows a perspective grid over the page. While it is on, every object a drawing tool makes (rectangles, ellipses, polygons, curves, brush strokes, text frames) is laid onto the active plane of the grid. Objects you paste, duplicate or move with the Pick tool stay as they are. The bar at the top left of the drawing window has: Finish: leaves the mode; the objects keep their perspective; 1-Point, 2-Point and 3-Point: the kind of grid; the planes: Ground, Left, Right (and Top for a 1-point grid). The active plane is drawn strongly; Grid: shows the grid lines; Depth (5 to 98%): how far the grid reaches towards the vanishing points; Put on plane: lays the selected objects onto the active plane. Drag the vanishing points (circles) and the near corners (squares) to change the grid. An object laid on a plane gets an ordinary perspective effect, whose four corners you can still edit with the Shape tool.

h: Copying an effect Cloning an effect
x: Copying and cloning effects Instead of setting up an effect again, you can copy it from an object that already has it. Copying an effect Select the objects that should get the effect. Choose Object > Copy Effect and the kind of effect: Drop Shadow From, Transparency From, Envelope From, Perspective From, Distortion From, Extrude From, Contour From, Blend From, Lens From, Bevel From or Block Shadow From. Click the object to copy from. A right-click cancels. The effect is fitted to each object: an envelope or perspective is stretched to its size, a distortion keeps its center at the same place within it. When the object you click has no such effect, nothing changes and the status bar says so. The copy is one undo step. Cloning an effect Object > Clone Effect copies the shadow (Shadow From) or the transparency (Transparency From) of another object, and keeps following it: change the source and the clones change too, until you edit a clone's own effect. Edit > Clone makes a clone of a whole object, and Copy Properties From copies the fill, outline or text properties of another object.

h: Vector Mosaic Picture Mosaic
x: Vector and picture mosaics A mosaic rebuilds the selected objects, or a picture, out of many small tiles. A vector mosaic uses colored shapes; a picture mosaic uses photos from a folder of your own. Vector Mosaic Open the Vector Mosaic panel with Effects > Vector Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to turn into a mosaic. Set the options: Density: tiles per inch (10 at first); Scale: the size of each tile within its cell (1 at first); Screen angle: how the rows are turned (30 degrees at first). Keep original: off deletes the selection once the mosaic is made. Limit colors: reduce the tiles to at most that many colors (16 at first). Method: Uniform (every tile full size, transparency flattened on white), Size modulation 1 (the tile size follows the opacity, at first) or Size modulation 2 (darker areas give bigger tiles). Merge adjacent: combine up to that many neighbouring tiles of one color; Weld adjacent overlap: one curve per color instead of one object per tile. Shape: circle (at first), square or custom. For a custom tile, select a closed curve and click Select. Click Apply. The mosaic is one group placed on top of the selection, and is selected. Picture Mosaic Open the Picture Mosaic panel with Effects > Picture Mosaic.  Select the objects or bitmaps to rebuild. Under Library, click Browse and choose a folder of pictures (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, WebP or TIFF; up to 1000). The panel shows how many it holds. Set the options: Keep original (on at first). Columns: tiles across (30 at first); the rows follow from the shape of the selection. Blending: how much of the selection shows over the tiles (20% at first). Allow duplicates (on), with the tile spacing: the fewest tiles between two uses of one picture. Composition: single, stack or array; Edges: stretch the last row or remove it; Output priority and the resolution: how large the mosaic is in pixels. The panel shows the resulting size. Click Apply. Note: Picture libraries need the desktop version; the browser version cannot read folders.

h: To apply a bitmap effect The effect groups Special dialogs Editing the effects of an object The Effect Picker Effects that spread past the edges
x: Bitmap effects Bitmap effects change pixels: blur, sharpen, adjust colors, add textures and artistic strokes. They work on bitmaps and also on vector objects, which are then drawn as the picture the effects make while keeping their own shape, fill and outline. Effects are kept apart from the original pixels: you can edit, hide, reorder or remove any of them later, and removing the last one gives the original back. To apply a bitmap effect Select one or more objects. Choose a group in the Effects menu and an effect. Effects without settings apply at once. The others open a dialog box with before and after previews of the first selected object: set the values and click OK. Reset puts every setting back to its default.  The change to the whole selection is one undo step. With a bitmap selected, Ctrl+B opens Brightness/Contrast/Intensity, Ctrl+Shift+B Color Balance and Ctrl+Shift+U Hue/Saturation/Lightness. The effect groups 3D Effects Cylinder, Emboss, Page Curl, Pinch/Punch, Sphere Adjust Auto Adjust, Image Adjustments, Contrast Enhancement, Local Equalization, Target Color Balance, Tone Curve, Brightness/Contrast/Intensity, Color Balance, Gamma, Hue/Saturation/Lightness, Selective Color, Replace Colors, Desaturate, Channel Mixer Art Strokes Charcoal, Conté Crayon, Crayon, Cubist, Impressionist, Palette Knife, Pastels, Pen & Ink, Pointillist, Scraperboard, Sketch Pad, Watercolor, Felt Marker, Paper Grain Blur Directional Smooth, Gaussian Blur, Smooth Jagged Edges, Low Pass, Motion Blur, Radial Blur, Smart Blur, Smooth, Soften, Zoom Camera Colorize, Diffuse, Photo Filter, Sepia Toning, Vintage Photo Color Transform Bit Planes, Halftone, Psychedelic, Solarize Contour Edge Detect, Find Edges, Trace Contour Correction Dust and Scratch Creative Crystallize, Fabric, Frame, Glass Tiles, Mosaic, Scatter, Tinted Glass, Stained Glass, Vignette, Vortex Custom Bump Map Distort Blocks, Displace, Mesh Warp, Offset, Pixelate, Ripple, Swirl, Tile, Wet Paint, Whirlpool, Wind Noise Add Noise, Maximum, Median, Minimum, Remove Moiré, Remove Noise Sharpen Adaptive Unsharp, Directional Sharpen, High Pass, Sharpen, Unsharp Mask Texture Cobblestone, Wrinkles, Etching, Plastic, Relief Sculpture, Stone Transform Deinterlace, Invert Colors, Posterize Special dialogs Image Adjustments opens a larger dialog box: a large preview you can zoom, pan and rotate, shown alone, side by side or split; Auto adjust and pickers for the white and black points; sliders for temperature, tint, saturation, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows and midtones, with a histogram; undo and redo inside the dialog; and snapshots of settings to compare. Contrast Enhancement shows the histogram with markers to drag for the input and output levels, eyedroppers for black and white, and Auto adjust. Tone Curve edits a curve per channel (master, red, green, blue) in four styles (curve, straight, freehand, gamma), over the histogram; curves can be saved and loaded. Colors of the picture, such as in Replace Colors, have an eyedropper: click a preview to take the color under the pointer. Editing the effects of an object The FX section of the Properties panel lists the effects of the selected object, first applied at the top. Each row has a check box to show or hide the effect, Edit (opens its dialog box), Move up, Move down and Delete. Add effect opens the effect groups. Effects > Flatten Effects makes the effects permanent: a bitmap keeps what it shows, and a vector object becomes a bitmap. The Effect Picker Effects > Effect Picker opens a window that stays open while you work, with every effect as a small picture. Type in the search field to find effects, or choose a group or Recent from the list. With something selected, click a tile to apply the effect. You can also apply an effect as a lens. Effects that spread past the edges Blurs and similar effects can reach past the edges of a bitmap. With Bitmaps > Inflate Bitmap > Auto Inflate Bitmap on (as at first), the bitmap grows to make room for them. See Resampling and straightening. To save a bitmap with its effects as a PNG file, right-click it and choose Save Bitmap As.

Tekst TraceDraw kent twee soorten tekst. Artistieke tekst is een regel, of een paar regels, op een punt: titels, labels, logo's. Alineatekst loopt in een kader en breekt af aan de randen: lopende tekst, kolommen, lijsten. Beide kunnen teken voor teken worden opgemaakt, langs paden worden gezet en op spelling worden gecontroleerd. Deze pagina's leggen uit hoe u tekst toevoegt en opmaakt, alinea's vormgeeft, lettertypen en speciale tekens kiest, en de schrijfhulpmiddelen gebruikt.

h: Adding text Editing text Formatting from the property bar The Text panel Paragraph text frames Moving and turning characters Text on a path Other text commands
x: Adding and editing text Adding text Choose the Text tool (F8). For artistic text, click where the text starts and type. Press Enter to start a new line. For paragraph text, drag a frame, then type. The text wraps at the edges of the frame. Press Esc to finish. An empty text is removed. New artistic text is 24 points, paragraph text 12 points, in the first sans-serif font found. Change the defaults by formatting with nothing selected. To make an existing object a text frame, right-click it and choose to create an empty text frame; see Empty frames. Text > Insert Placeholder Text fills the selected frames with sample text, as much as fits. Editing text Click text with the Text tool, or double-click it with the Pick tool, to edit it in place. Text > Edit Text (Ctrl+Shift+T) does the same. Typing, Ctrl+V insert at the caret, replacing the selection Backspace, Delete delete the selection, else the character before or after Enter, Shift+Enter new paragraph, new line Arrow keys, with Ctrl move by a character or a word; Shift selects Home, End, with Ctrl start or end of the line, or of the text Ctrl+A select all Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U bold, italic, underline Double-click select a word All your typing in one editing session is one undo step. Formatting from the property bar With the Text tool, or with text selected, the property bar has the font list, the size (type it or pick from the list), bold, italic, underline, the alignment (left, center, right, full justify), bullets and drop cap for paragraph text, Text (Ctrl+T) and Edit Text. While editing, they act on the selected characters; otherwise on the whole selected texts. Your choice also becomes the default for the next text. The font list shows each family in its own font, with the ones you used last at the top. Type to narrow the list. A family with several styles has an arrow that shows them. See Fonts and glyphs. The Text panel The Text panel (Ctrl+T) has every text setting, in three sections you can open and close: Character, Paragraph and Frame. The three buttons at the top show the panel from that section on.  Character: the font, style and size; range kerning (-50 to 200%) and underline; the fill, background and outline of the characters. More options under the section: character offsets and angle, strikethrough and OpenType features. Paragraph: the alignment (none, left, center, right, full justify, and forced justify, which spreads the last line too); line spacing in percent of the character height, points or percent of the font size; left, first-line and right indents; space before and after paragraphs; character and word spacing. The gear opens custom hyphens. Frame, for paragraph text: the background color of the frame, the vertical alignment (top, middle, bottom), fit text to frame, columns (1 to 8) and the gap between them, and links to the bullets, drop cap and columns dialog boxes, and hyphenation. Every change applies to the selected characters while editing, or to the selected texts, and is one undo step. With no text selected, the settings become those of new text. The button at the top right gives new text the settings of the selected text. Paragraph text frames Frames show as dashed lines. A frame turns red, with a small tab under its bottom edge, when its text does not fit; the text that does not fit is not drawn, printed or exported. To make it fit: drag the frame's handles to enlarge it. The text flows again; the letters keep their size; choose Text > Paragraph Text Frame > Fit Text to Frame to resize the text to fill the frame; link the frame to another one, so the text flows on: Link. Unlink breaks the link. Text > Show Text Frames shows or hides the frames. Moving and turning characters With the Shape tool, text shows a node at each character: drag nodes to move characters, and drag the arrows at the corners of the text to change the character, word and line spacing. The character offsets and angle can also be typed in the Text panel. Text > Straighten Text puts characters back in line, and Align to Baseline (Alt+F12) removes their vertical offsets. Text on a path Select a text and a curve or shape. Choose Text > Fit Text to Path. Or click the outline of a path with the Text tool and type. Text on a closed shape stands on its outside, centered on its top. With text on a path selected, the property bar sets the orientation of the letters (rotated, vertical or horizontal skew, or upright), the vertical placement (on the baseline, ascender, descender or center), the placement along the path, the distance and offset, and mirroring. Drag the text to slide it along the path. Straighten Text takes it off the path. Other text commands Text > Insert Formatting Code: special characters such as Em Space, Non-breaking Space, Optional Hyphen and Column/Frame Break. Show Non-Printing Characters shows spaces, tabs and breaks. Make Text Web-compatible prepares text for web pages. Text > Convert switches between artistic and paragraph text. Converting text to curves (Object > Convert to Curves) keeps its look without the font. Text files can be imported; see Importing files.

t: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps
h: Tabs Columns Bullets Drop caps Hyphenation
x: Tabs, columns, bullets and drop caps The Text menu has four dialog boxes for laying out paragraph text. Each acts on the selected paragraph text. Their settings are also in the Frame section of the Text panel. Tabs Text > Tabs sets where the Tab character jumps to. At first there is a tab stop every 12.7 mm (half an inch). Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Tabs. Under Tab stops, change the positions, or click Add tab to add one. Click Close.  Columns Text > Columns splits a text frame into columns; the text flows from one column into the next. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Columns. Set the number of Columns and the Gutter, the space between columns (5 mm at first). Click Close.  To break to the next column at a given place, insert Column/Frame Break from Insert Formatting Code. Bullets Text > Bullets puts a bullet before each paragraph. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Bullets. Tick Use bullets, and set the bullet Symbol and the Indent (5 mm at first). Click Close.  Drop caps A drop cap is a large first letter that spans several lines. Select the paragraph text. Choose Text > Drop Cap. Tick Use drop cap and set the Lines dropped (3 at first). Click Close. The letter is scaled so its top meets the top of the first line and it sits on the baseline of the last line it spans; the lines beside it are shortened to make room.  Hyphenation Text > Use Hyphenation lets words break at the end of lines, with at least two letters before and three after the break. Words with a capital letter are never broken. To decide yourself where a word may break, see Custom hyphens.

h: The Fonts panel Missing fonts The Font Sampler The Glyphs panel The Font Manager
x: Fonts and glyphs TraceDraw uses the fonts installed on your computer, fonts you add in the Font Manager, and fonts that come with a drawing. This page explains the panels and the dialog box for working with fonts and special characters. The Fonts panel The Fonts panel lists the font families.  Type in the filter field to narrow the list. Under Fonts in document are the families the drawing uses. A family that is not installed is marked missing; its text shows in a similar font and keeps its font name. A family that came with the drawing is marked embedded. Click a family to give it to the selected text, or to make it the font of new text. Missing fonts When a drawing uses fonts that are not installed, a message names them after it opens (see Notes after opening). Install the fonts and the text shows in them again. Drawings saved as .tdraw, and .cdr files with embedded fonts, can carry their fonts along. The Font Sampler The Font Sampler panel (Text > Font Sampler) shows a line of sample text in several fonts, one under the other, to compare them.  Type the sample text at the top; left empty, a sentence in your interface language is used. Set the size (10 to 96, 28 at first). Add fonts by typing part of a name and clicking one of the matches (up to 24 fonts); the cross removes one. At first the panel lists the text font and the fonts of the drawing. Click a sample to give that font to the selected text. The Glyphs panel The Glyphs panel (Text > Glyphs, Ctrl+F11) shows every character of a font, to insert symbols and special characters.  Choose the font. Choose a character range: the entire font, Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, punctuation, numbers, currency, arrows, mathematical operators or symbols. Click a character. It is inserted at the caret of the text you are editing, or as a new text in the middle of the page. Hover a character to see its name and code. A small arrow under a character means the font has alternates for it (such as swashes or small capitals); click it to see them. The glyphs you used last are at the top of the panel. The Font Manager Tools > Font Manager opens the Font Manager, a window that organizes your fonts.  Libraries (top left): My fonts (the installed fonts), the folders you added, Favorites and your collections. Double-click a collection to rename it; right-click for more. Filters (bottom left): by status (installed, not installed, protected system fonts, duplicates), embedding rights, technology (TrueType, OpenType, variable), weight, width, style, character range and OpenType features. Clear removes them. Right side: the sample text and its presets, a search field (family, style or PostScript name), and the fonts as cards, grouped by family. Each card shows a sample, the technology and a bar that is green when the font is installed. Click to pick a font, Ctrl+click to pick several. To use the Font Manager: Add folder scans a folder for font files (TTF, OTF, TTC, OTC); its fonts show as not installed. Add font installs one file at once. Install makes the picked fonts available in TraceDraw, now and at every start. Uninstall removes them; the system's own fonts are protected. Add to collection and Remove from collection organize fonts; drag fonts onto Favorites or a collection to add them. Double-click an installed font, or choose Use in drawing, to give it to the selected text. Show details shows the family, style, version, file, technology, embedding rights, weight, width, glyph count, scripts and features of the font you clicked. Fonts the drawing uses that are not installed are listed in orange above the cards. In the browser version, Add font loads a font file for the session only.

h: The Writing Tools dialog box Spell Checker Grammar Thesaurus Autocorrect Custom hyphens Change case Text statistics Encode Web-compatible text
x: Writing tools TraceDraw checks spelling and grammar, finds synonyms, corrects as you type, and fixes text that came in with the wrong characters. The commands are in Text > Writing Tools and the Text menu. The Writing Tools dialog box Text > Writing Tools > Spell Check, Grammar and Thesaurus open the Writing Tools dialog box at that tab. Check chooses whether to check every text of the page (Document) or only the selected texts (Selection).  Spell Checker Click Start. The first word not found shows, with suggestions under Replacements. Click a suggestion to put it in Replace with (double-click to replace at once), or type the right word. Click Replace for this place, Auto Replace for every place, Skip Once or Skip All to leave it, or Add to add the word to your own word list. Undo takes back the last replacement. Options has Ignore words with numbers and Ignore words in capitals. TraceDraw uses the dictionaries installed on your system; without one, only a built-in word list is used. Grammar The grammar checker finds doubled words, double spaces, spaces before punctuation, missing spaces after it, sentences that start in lower case, unbalanced brackets and quotes, repeated punctuation, sentences over 40 words, missing end marks and, in English, "a" and "an" before the wrong sound. For each finding it shows the replacement, the New sentence and the Rule Name. Click Start (then Replace), Skip Once or Skip Rule. Thesaurus Type a word (the first word of the selected text at first) and click Look Up. The meanings show with their synonyms: click one to pick it, double-click to look it up. Insert puts it in the text, keeping the capitals. Under Options, Close after inserting closes the dialog box after inserting, and Choose Thesaurus File uses a thesaurus file you have. Autocorrect Text > Writing Tools > Autocorrect sets what is corrected while you type: Correct while typing; Capitalize first letter of sentences; Correct two initial capitals ("THe" becomes "The"); Use typographic quotation marks, in the style of your interface language; the Replacement table: (c) becomes ©, (r) ®, (tm) ™, 1/2 ½ and so on. Add and Remove change the rows. Apply to Selection applies the rules to the selected text. Text you paste or import is never changed.  Custom hyphens Text > Custom Optional Hyphens (also the gear of the Paragraph section of the Text panel) defines where your own words may break, such as product names. Those words break only there when hyphenation is on. Choose the Language (Show all languages lists every one). Type the Word and the Hyphenated Word with hyphens where it may break, such as Trace-Draw. Click Add Definition. Remove Definition removes the selected definition. Under Automatically insert custom optional hyphens, When typing and When pasting and importing text turn hyphenation on for texts that hold a defined word. Click Apply to Selection to apply them to the selected text now, or OK to keep them.  Change case Text > Change Case changes the selected text to Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Title Case or tOGGLE cASE.  Text statistics Text > Text Statistics counts the text objects, lines, words, characters and fonts of the selected text, or of the page.  Encode Text that came from another program sometimes shows the wrong characters, such as "cafÃ©" instead of "café". Text > Encode fixes it: Select the text. Choose how the text Text was read as and what It really is (UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1, Mac OS Roman or Windows-1251). Check the Preview and click OK.  Web-compatible text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies the selected text for web pages: gradient, pattern, texture and mesh fills become a flat color, and outlines, shadows and effects are removed.

Sjablonen en stijlen Sjablonen en stijlen besparen werk dat u anders zou herhalen. Een sjabloon is een kant-en-klare tekening om mee te beginnen. Een stijl is een benoemde set van vulling, omtrek en transparantie die gekoppeld blijft aan de objecten die hem gebruiken, zodat één wijziging ze allemaal aanpast. De standaardeigenschappen bepalen hoe nieuwe objecten eruitzien. Kleurstijlen, die voor losse kleuren op dezelfde manier werken, worden uitgelegd in Kleurstijlen.

h: Starting from a template The built-in templates Saving your own templates
x: Templates A template is a drawing to start from: a blank page of a common size, or a designed business card, flyer, poster, letterhead or label to fill in. Opening a template makes a new, untitled drawing; the template itself never changes. Starting from a template Choose File > New from Template, or click New from Template on the Welcome Screen. Find a template: type in Search templates to match names and categories; choose where templates come from: All templates, Built in or My templates; choose a category, or All categories. Click a template to see it. With Show template details on, the pane on the right shows it large with its Category, Page size and Source. Click Open, double-click the template, or press Enter. The Size slider at the bottom makes the thumbnails larger or smaller, and Open template opens any .tdt or .tdraw file as a template.  The built-in templates Blank pages: A4 portrait and landscape, A3, Letter, business card (90 by 50 mm), A2 poster, web (1920 by 1080 pixels) and social media (1080 by 1080 pixels). Designed: two business cards, a sale flyer and an event flyer, a poster, a letterhead, a certificate, an invoice, a birthday banner, a quote post and a round label. They are made of ordinary shapes and text with sample text, so you can change every part. Saving your own templates Make the drawing you want to start from in the future. Choose File > Save as Template. Give it a name and save it. Templates you save appear under My templates. They are kept in the templates folder of your settings, so they are not available in the browser version.

h: Default properties Changing defaults with nothing selected Styles To make a style Using and changing styles
x: Object styles and default properties The Object Styles panel has two parts: the Default Properties of new objects, and the styles of the drawing. Both are saved with the drawing. Open it from Window > Panels, or right-click an object and choose the object styles panel.  Default properties New objects take the fill and outline of their kind: Graphic: shapes, lines, tables and everything except text no fill, a thin black outline Artistic text: text without a frame black fill, no outline Paragraph text: text in a frame black fill, no outline In the panel, each kind shows its fill and outline, with From Selection (take the fill and outline of the selected object) and Reset (back to the defaults of a new drawing). Changing defaults with nothing selected When nothing is selected and you choose a fill or outline (click a palette color, use a fill tool, change the outline color or width), the change goes to new objects. TraceDraw asks which kinds of new objects it applies to: Tick Graphic, Artistic text and Paragraph text as needed. The kinds you ticked last time are ticked. Tick Use these kinds from now on without asking to skip the question from now on. Click OK. Cancel changes nothing.  The check box Ask which kinds a change with nothing selected applies to in the panel turns the question on or off. The Properties panel with nothing selected also edits the Graphic defaults. To keep the defaults for every new drawing, choose Tools > Save Settings as Default. Styles A style is a named set of properties: Fill, Outline (its color, width, line style and arrowheads) and Transparency. Objects you give a style stay linked to it: change the style and they all change. To make a style Select an object with the look you want. Click New style from selection. The style is named "Style 1" and so on, takes the fill, outline and transparency of the object, and is linked to every selected object. Using and changing styles Each style shows its swatches, its name (click it to rename), how many objects are linked to it, and its parts as check boxes: Apply gives the selection the style and links it. Update from selection takes the fill, outline and transparency of the selected object; every linked object follows. Turning a part off leaves that property to each object. Delete removes the style; linked objects keep their look. Break Link to Style unlinks the selected objects, which keep their look. You can still change a linked object directly; the next change of its style sets the style's parts again. Right-click an object to apply a style from its menu.

Pagina's en lay-out Een tekening kan veel pagina's hebben, elk met een eigen formaat en stand. Deze pagina's leggen uit hoe u pagina's toevoegt, ordent en nummert, de documentopties instelt (paginaformaat, lay-out, achtergrond, afloop, linialen, raster en hulplijnen), hulplijnen plaatst, objecten laat uitlijnen en de eigenschappen van een tekening leest.

h: Moving between pages The Pages panel Inserting pages Duplicating a page Renaming a page Page size and orientation Page numbers Page background
x: Working with pages Moving between pages Click a page tab under the drawing window, or use the page navigator beside them (first, previous, next and last page). Press PgUp or PgDn. Choose Layout > Go to Page, type the page number in the Go To Page dialog box and click OK.  The Pages panel The Pages panel lists the pages of the drawing. Click a page to go to it. Its buttons Insert Page, Delete Page and Duplicate Page act on the current page, and Page Sorter View shows every page as a thumbnail. Open it from Window > Panels.  Inserting pages Choose Layout > Insert Page, or click one of the insert buttons of the page navigator (they add one page of the current size before or after the current page at once). In the Insert Page dialog box, set the Number of pages and choose Before or After the current page. Click OK.  Delete Page deletes pages. Duplicating a page Choose Layout > Duplicate Page, or right-click the page tab and choose Duplicate Page. Under Insert new page, choose Before selected page or After selected page. Choose Copy layer(s) only for a page with the same layers and nothing on them, or Copy layer(s) and their contents to copy the objects too. Click OK. The copy becomes the current page; Edit > Undo removes it. The page tab menu also has Insert Page After, Insert Page Before, Delete Page and Switch Page Orientation. Renaming a page Choose Layout > Rename Page, or double-click the page tab. Type the Page name and click OK.  Page size and orientation Layout > Page Size opens the Page Size dialog box: Type the Width and Height; Swap exchanges them. Tick Apply to all pages to change every page, or leave it off to change the current page only. Click OK.  Switch Page Orientation turns the page between portrait and landscape. With nothing selected, the property bar of the Pick tool also sets the page size and orientation. The full page settings are in Document options. Page numbers Layout > Insert Page Number puts a page number On Active Layer, On All Pages, On All Odd Pages or On All Even Pages. The numbers on master layers show the right number on every page. Object > Insert > Page Number places one in the text you are editing. Layout > Page Number Settings sets how they look: Start at: the first number; Prefix and Suffix: text around the number, such as "Page "; Style: 1, 2, 3, I, II, III, i, ii, iii, A, B, C or a, b, c; Position: Bottom centre, Bottom outer corner, Top centre or Top outer corner.  Page background Layout > Page Background sets the color behind every page; see Document options.

h: The layout Working in multipage view
x: Multipage view View > Multipage View lays every page of the drawing out on the desktop at once, so you can compare pages and edit them side by side. The layout The pages sit in a grid, in page order: two columns for up to four pages, three for up to nine, and so on. Each page shows its number and name below it; the current page's are in the normal text color, the others dimmed. Working in multipage view The current page is edited as usual: rulers, guidelines, grids and the status bar refer to it. Click or drag on another page to make it current and work there at once. The page tabs and the navigator change the current page too. Zoom To Fit (F4) fits every page in the window. Choose Multipage View again to go back to one page at a time. Page Sorter View shows the pages as thumbnails instead; the two views exclude each other.

h: General Page size Layout Background Bleed Rulers Grid Guidelines
x: Document options Layout > Document Options opens the settings of the active drawing: page size, layout, background, bleed, rulers, grid and guidelines. Double-clicking a ruler or the page border also opens it. Choose a page from the list on the left. Changes show at once; OK keeps them and Cancel puts everything back. Save as default keeps the grid, ruler and guideline settings for new drawings. General  Rendering resolution: the resolution of effects that are turned into pixels, such as drop shadows and bitmap effects. Fill open curves (off at first): when on, open curves show their fill as if they were closed. Auto inflate bitmaps for effects (on at first): bitmaps grow to make room for effects that spread past their edges. Duplicate offset: how far Duplicate places the copy. Page size  Choose Page size for a paper size, or Label presets for sheets of labels, which set the page to the sheet size and add guidelines around each label. Size, Width and Height, and Portrait or Landscape. Apply size to current page only: change the current page only. Show page border, and Add Page Frame, which adds a rectangle the size of the page. Rendering resolution, Bleed and Show bleed area (see below). Layout  The page shows how many pages the drawing has, with Page Sorter View and Switch Page Orientation, and lists the Master layers, each shown on All pages, Odd pages or Even pages. The buttons add a new master layer for all, odd or even pages. See Master layers. Background  Choose No background, a Solid color, or a Bitmap (Choose bitmap) to show behind every page. Bleed  Bleed is the part of the drawing that runs past the edge of the page, so the print has no white edge once trimmed. Set the Bleed distance and tick Show bleed area to see it. Printing and PDF export can include the bleed; see Printing. Rulers  Units: the drawing units (inches, millimeters, picas, points, pixels, ciceros, didots, feet, yards, miles, centimeters, meters or kilometers). Drawing scale: makes a distance on the page stand for a distance in the world, such as 1:100. Choose a typical scale, or type the page distance and the world distance. Rulers, positions, sizes and new dimension lines then show world distances; page sizes, outline widths and text sizes do not. Origin: where the rulers count from (Horizontal and Vertical); Reset origin to the page corner puts it back. You can also drag the origin out of the corner where the rulers meet. Tick divisions: the number of ticks between ruler numbers. Nudge: the Nudge distance of the arrow keys (2.54 mm), the Super nudge with Shift (5.08 mm) and the Micro nudge with Ctrl (0.254 mm). Show rulers. Grid  Document grid: Show grid, Snap to grid, the Horizontal and Vertical spacing (10 mm at first), as a distance or as lines per unit, and Show grid as Lines or Dots. Baseline grid: lines across the page for lining up text, with the Baseline grid spacing (14 points), the Start from top (12.7 mm) and the Line color. Pixel grid: the Color and Opacity of the grid of pixels, Show grid at 800% or higher zoom and Snap to pixels. Guidelines  Show guidelines and Snap to guidelines. Default guideline color and Default preset guideline color. Presets: one inch margins, bleed area, page borders, printable area, a three-column newsletter, a basic grid and an upper left grid. User defined: Margins (Top, Bottom, Left, Right), Columns (Number of columns and Distance between) and a Grid (Rows and Columns). Apply Presets adds them; a line that is already there is not added twice. See Rulers, grids and guidelines for working with guidelines on the page.

h: Rulers The document grid Guidelines The Guidelines panel
x: Rulers, grids and guidelines Rulers, grids and guidelines help you place objects precisely. None of them print. Rulers The rulers run along the top and left of the drawing window, in the drawing units; View > Rulers shows or hides them. A dashed line on each ruler follows the pointer. Drag from the corner where the rulers meet to move the origin, the point the rulers count from. Positions on the property bar, the status bar and in the panels count from it too. Drag from a ruler to add a guideline. Double-click a ruler to open its settings; see Document options, where you also set the units and the drawing scale. The document grid View > Grid > Document Grid shows a grid of lines or dots over the page, behind the objects; Document Grid in Snap To makes objects snap to it. Its spacing (10 mm at first) is set in Document options. When lines would be too close, only every second, fifth or tenth line is drawn. The baseline grid (Baseline Grid) draws lines across the page like a ruled notebook, for lining up text; the pixel grid (Pixel Grid) shows the pixels of the drawing in the Pixels view from 800% zoom. Guidelines Guidelines are lines across the drawing window that objects can snap to. Drag from the top ruler for a horizontal guideline, from the left ruler for a vertical one. With the Pick tool, click a guideline to select it (Shift+click adds), and drag it to move it. Drop it outside the drawing window, or press Delete, to delete it. Click the selected guideline again to show its rotation handles, and drag them to turn it. Right-click a guideline to delete, lock or unlock it, or open its properties. Locked guidelines can be selected but not moved or deleted. Edit > Select All > Guidelines selects every guideline of the page, and Guidelines shows or hides them. The Guidelines panel The Guidelines panel places guidelines by their coordinates. Open it from Window > Panels.  Show and Snap turn guidelines on and snapping to them. Choose the Guideline type: horizontal, vertical or angled. Type the position (x, y, and the Angle for an angled one), counted from the ruler origin. Click Add to add a guideline, or select one in the list and click Modify to move it. The list shows the page's guidelines of that type (Ctrl+click to select several). Delete, Lock and Unlock act on the selected ones, and Guideline color and Guideline style (Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash dot) change their look. Ready-made sets of guidelines (margins, columns, grids) are on the Guidelines page of the document options.

h: Turning snapping on and off What objects snap to Snapping while moving Dynamic and alignment guides
x: Snapping Snapping pulls the pointer, and the objects you move, onto exact points: nodes, the middles of segments, the centers of shapes, guidelines, the grid or the page. It makes it easy to join lines and line objects up without zooming in. Turning snapping on and off View > Snap To, or the Snap To list on the standard toolbar, turns snapping to Pixels, Document Grid (Ctrl+Y), Baseline Grid, Guidelines, Objects (Alt+Z) and Page on and off. At first objects, guidelines and the page are on. Snap Off (Alt+Q) turns all snapping off and on again. What objects snap to When snapping to objects is on, these points attract the pointer within the snapping radius (10 screen pixels at first). Each shows its mark and, with screen tips on, its name. Node the nodes of outlines, the corners of rectangles, the points of polygons Intersection where two outlines cross Midpoint halfway along each segment Quadrant the top, bottom, left and right of ellipses Tangent where a line you draw touches an ellipse or curve Perpendicular where a line you draw meets a segment at a right angle Edge the nearest point of an outline Center the center of shapes, bitmaps and tables Text baseline the baseline of a line of text Points win over guidelines, guidelines over the grids, and edges come last. The modes, the radius and the marks are set on the Snapping page of the options; see TraceDraw options. Snapping while moving When you start moving a selection with the Pick tool on one of its points (a node, a midpoint or the center), that point is carried onto the other object's point or edge. Otherwise the edges and center of the selection's box snap to guidelines, grids, the page and other objects. The handles snap while you resize. Dynamic and alignment guides View > Dynamic Guides (Alt+Shift+D) shows temporary guides at 0, 45, 90 and 135 degrees through the points you pass over, so you can draw along them. Alignment Guides (Alt+Shift+A) shows guides when the object you move lines up with others.

h: Describing the drawing The report
x: Document properties File > Document Properties opens the Document Properties dialog box. It keeps information about the drawing, such as its title and author, and reports everything the drawing holds.  Describing the drawing Language: the language of the drawing's text, or none. PDF files written from the drawing carry it, which helps screen readers. Title, Subject, Author, Copyright, Tags (keywords written to PDF and SVG files) and Notes (several lines). Rating: none or one to five stars. Click OK to keep the changes, as one undo step. Cancel leaves everything as it was. The title, subject and rating can also be set when you save; see Save As. The report Under the fields, a report lists what the drawing holds, in sections: File: the name and location of the file. Document: the pages and layers, the page size (in the drawing units and in pixels), the orientation and the resolution. Color: the color profiles, the primary color mode and the rendering intent. Graphic Objects: the number of objects and of points, the most points and parts one curve has, and the curves, rectangles, ellipses, polygons, groups and tables. Text Statistics: artistic and paragraph texts, characters, words and the fonts used. Bitmap Objects: the number of bitmaps, their total pixels and the largest one. Styles: object and color styles. Effects: each effect, with how many objects use it. Fills and Outlines: the objects by kind of fill and outline, and how many use each color model. Symbols: symbols defined and instances placed. The report helps before sending a file to print: for example, it shows which fonts the drawing needs and whether it holds RGB colors. For a full check, see Preflight.

Bitmaps Bitmaps zijn afbeeldingen van pixels, zoals foto's en scans. TraceDraw plaatst ze in tekeningen, wijzigt hun kleurmodus en formaat, zet ze recht, maskeert kleuren, past effecten toe en vectoriseert ze tot vormen. Het zet ook vectorobjecten om in bitmaps. Gebruik Bestand > Importeren om een afbeelding binnen te halen; zie Bestanden importeren. Met een bitmap geselecteerd heeft de eigenschappenbalk de bitmapopdrachten: bewerken, bijsnijden, vectoriseren, rechtzetten en herbemonsteren. Voor effecten, zie Bitmapeffecten.

h: Instellingen
x: Objecten naar bitmaps omzetten Bitmaps > Converteren naar bitmap (ook Object > Converteren naar bitmap) maakt van de geselecteerde objecten één bitmap. Gebruik het om complex tekenwerk plat te maken of om objecten voor te bereiden op bitmapeffecten. Het is één ongedaan-makenstap.  Instellingen Resolutie: kies uit de lijst (72 tot 600 dpi) of typ een waarde (36 tot 2400; in het begin 300). Kleurmodus: Zwart-wit (1-bits), Grijswaarden (8-bits), Palet (8-bits), RGB-kleur (24-bits, in het begin) of CMYK-kleur (32-bits). Dithering: bij Zwart-wit en Palet worden stippen gemengd om de ontbrekende tinten te suggereren. Zwart altijd overdrukken: het zwart van de bitmap wordt over de kleuren eronder gedrukt. Anti-aliasing (in het begin aan): vloeiende randen; uit geeft harde pixelranden. Transparante achtergrond (in het begin aan); uit plaatst de objecten op wit. Het dialoogvenster toont hoe groot de bitmap ongecomprimeerd wordt.

h: Zwart-wit Duotoon Palet Zwart-witbitmaps kleuren
x: De kleurmodus van bitmaps wijzigen Bitmaps > Modus zet de geselecteerde bitmaps om naar een andere kleurmodus. Elke geselecteerde bitmap verandert in één ongedaan-makenstap en de transparantie blijft behouden. De modi met instellingen openen een dialoogvenster met een voorbeeld vooraf en achteraf. Zwart-wit (1-bits) alleen zwart en wit (zie hieronder) Grijswaarden (8-bits) grijstinten Duotoon (8-bits) één tot vier inkten (zie hieronder) Palet (8-bits) maximaal 256 kleuren (zie hieronder) RGB-kleur (24-bits) de pixels zoals ze zijn Lab-kleur (24-bits) Lab-kleur CMYK-kleur (32-bits) de pixels zoals ze zijn; kleurbeheer zet ze om bij de uitvoer Zwart-wit  Kies de omzettingsmethode: Lijntekening: wit waar het grijs op of boven de drempel ligt (in het begin 128), elders zwart; Geordend: een regelmatig patroon van stippen; Halftoon (in het begin): een raster van ronde, lijnvormige of vierkante stippen onder een hoek (45 graden) en met een aantal lijnen per inch (60); Kardinaliteitsverdeling: een willekeurig ogende textuur; Jarvis, Stucki en Floyd-Steinberg: foutdiffusie, de vloeiendste resultaten voor foto's. Intensiteit (0 tot 100, in het begin 50) maakt het resultaat lichter of donkerder. Duotoon  Een duotoon drukt een grijswaardenafbeelding af met enkele inkten, wat rijke tinten geeft met weinig kleuren. Kies het type: Monotoon, Duotoon (in het begin), Tritoon of Quadtoon, voor één tot vier inkten. Klik op een inkt om de kleur ervan te wijzigen. Bewerk de curve: horizontaal staat het grijsniveau (zwart links), verticaal hoeveel van die inkt wordt afgedrukt. Sleep op een lege plek om een punt toe te voegen, sleep een punt om het te verplaatsen, dubbelklik erop of sleep het van het raster om het te verwijderen. Alles tonen tekent ook de curven van de andere inkten. Opslaan en Laden bewaren de inkten en curven in een bestand. Palet  Palet: Uniforme kleuren, Standaard VGA (16 kleuren), Adaptief en Geoptimaliseerd (de eigen kleuren van de afbeelding, teruggebracht tot het aantal kleuren dat u instelt, maximaal 256), Grijswaarden, Systeem of Aangepast (het documentpalet). Dithering: Geen, Geordend, Jarvis, Stucki of Floyd-Steinberg, met de ditheringintensiteit. Het resulterende palet verschijnt onder de instellingen. Zwart-witbitmaps kleuren Als alleen tweekleurige bitmaps geselecteerd zijn, klikt u op een paletkleur om hun achtergrond te kleuren en klikt u met de rechtermuisknop om hun voorgrond te kleuren.

h: Herbemonsteren Afbeelding rechtzetten Bitmaps vergroten Andere bitmapopdrachten
x: Bitmaps herbemonsteren, rechtzetten en vergroten Herbemonsteren Bitmaps > Opnieuw samplen geeft de geselecteerde bitmaps een nieuw aantal pixels; hun grootte op de pagina blijft gelijk.  Typ de nieuwe grootte in pixels, als percentage of als de resolutie die dat geeft bij de grootte op de pagina. Met Hoogte-breedteverhouding behouden aan volgt de hoogte de breedte. Kies de methode: Vloeiend (foto's), in het begin; Scherp, iets scherper; Harde pixels (pixelkunst): elke pixel blijft een vierkant van één kleur; Vergroten met detail: vloeiend, daarna verscherpt als de afbeelding groter wordt. Klik op OK. Het dialoogvenster toont de oorspronkelijke en de nieuwe grootte en het geheugen dat de nieuwe afbeelding inneemt. Als er meerdere bitmaps geselecteerd zijn, wordt elke bitmap met dezelfde factor geschaald. Afbeelding rechtzetten Bitmaps > Afbeelding rechtzetten corrigeert foto's die scheef staan, onder een hoek zijn genomen of door de lens zijn vervormd.  Gebruik het Raster (grootte en kleur zijn instelbaar) om de afbeelding uit te lijnen. Stel de schuifregelaars in: Lensvervorming corrigeren (-100 tot 100), Afbeelding draaien (-15 tot 15 graden), Verticaal perspectief en Horizontaal perspectief (-100 tot 100). De draaiknoppen draaien de afbeelding eerst een kwartslag. Met Afbeelding bijsnijden aan wordt het resultaat bijgesneden tot de grootste rechthoek met de oorspronkelijke verhoudingen; Bijsnijden en herbemonsteren naar oorspronkelijke grootte brengt het terug naar het oorspronkelijke aantal pixels. Zonder bijsnijden zijn de hoeken transparant. Klik op OK. Herstellen zet alle instellingen terug. Zoom en pan in het voorbeeld met de gereedschappen erboven. Het resultaat vervangt de pixels, dus effecten op de bitmap worden definitief. Bitmaps vergroten Sommige effecten, zoals vervagingen, reiken tot voorbij de randen van een bitmap. Bitmaps > Bitmap uitbreiden > Bitmap automatisch uitbreiden (in het begin aan) vergroot bitmaps met wat hun effecten nodig hebben, met een transparante marge. Bitmap handmatig uitbreiden vergroot de geselecteerde bitmaps met de hand: typ voor de breedte en hoogte de nieuwe grootte in pixels of als percentage (100 tot 1000%), met Hoogte-breedteverhouding behouden. De afbeelding blijft gecentreerd.  Andere bitmapopdrachten Bitmap bijsnijden snijdt een bitmap bij met het gereedschap Bijsnijden; een hoek van een bitmap slepen met het gereedschap Vorm snijdt hem ook bij. Bitmap bewerken opent de bitmap in een ander programma. Achtergrond verwijderen met AI maakt de achtergrond van een foto transparant. Achtergrond verwijderen: Achtergrond verwijderen. Koppeling verbreken en Bijwerken vanuit koppeling werken op bitmaps die aan een bestand gekoppeld zijn. Save Bitmap As slaat een bitmap op als PNG-bestand.

h: Snel overtrekken Het dialoogvenster Bitmap overtrekken
x: Bitmaps overtrekken Overtrekken zet een bitmap om in vectorvormen die u zonder kwaliteitsverlies kunt bewerken, herkleuren en schalen: een gescand logo, een schets, een foto. Snel overtrekken Selecteer een bitmap en kies Bitmaps > Snel overtrekken. Dit gebruikt de voorinstelling die is gekozen op de pagina Bitmaps overtrekken van de algemene opties (in het begin Illustratie). Het dialoogvenster Bitmap overtrekken Bitmaps > Omtrek overtrekken en Middenlijn overtrekken tonen voorinstellingen; kies er een om het dialoogvenster voor overtrekken te openen. Omtrek overtrekken vult kleurvlakken met vormen: Lijntekening, Logo, Gedetailleerd logo, Illustratie, Afbeelding van lage kwaliteit en Afbeelding van hoge kwaliteit. Middellijn overtrekken volgt lijnen met open curven: Technische illustratie en Pentekening.  Het dialoogvenster toont de bitmap vooraf en het overgetrokken resultaat achteraf, bijgewerkt terwijl u de instellingen wijzigt: de knoppen met voorinstellingen bovenaan; Detail (0 tot 100): meer detail behoudt kleinere vlakken; Gladmaken (0 tot 100, in het begin 25): vloeiendere curven, minder knooppunten; Gladheid van hoeken (0 tot 100): rondere hoeken; Zwart-wit, of het aantal Kleuren (1 tot 256); Achtergrond verwijderen (in het begin aan): laat de achtergrondkleur weg; Oorspronkelijke afbeelding verwijderen (in het begin uit); Voorbeeld telt de curven van het volledige resultaat. Klik op OK om over te trekken. De vormen worden over de bitmap geplaatst, de donkerste eerst.

h: Kleuren maskeren
x: Kleuren uit bitmaps maskeren Het paneel Bitmapmasker verbergt of behoudt de pixels van gekozen kleuren in een bitmap, bijvoorbeeld om een witte achtergrond transparant te maken. Open het met Bitmaps > Bitmapmasker.  Kleuren maskeren Selecteer een bitmap. Kies kleuren voor de tien kleurvakken: klik op de pipet en klik op kleuren in de bitmap; elke kleur vult het geselecteerde vak en vinkt het aan; of klik op Kleuren uit bitmap kiezen om de vakken te vullen met de tien kleuren die de bitmap het meest gebruikt. Selecteer een vak en stel de tolerantie in (0 tot 100%): hoe ver de kleur van een pixel van de kleur van het vak mag afwijken om toch overeen te komen. Kies Geselecteerde verbergen (overeenkomende pixels worden transparant) of Geselecteerde tonen (alleen overeenkomende pixels blijven, in het begin). Klik op Toepassen. Masker opslaan en Masker openen bewaren de vakken in een .msk-bestand; Verwijderen maakt het geselecteerde vak leeg. Elke bitmap verandert in één ongedaan-makenstap.

t: Removing the background of a bitmap
h: To remove a background Options Tips
x: Removing the background of a bitmap Bitmaps > Remove Background makes the background of a photo or scan transparent and keeps the subject. It works on this computer and needs no AI service. The property bar of a selected bitmap has the same command.  To remove a background Select one or more bitmaps. Click Bitmaps > Remove Background. The preview shows the bitmap before and after, with a checkerboard where it becomes transparent. Set the options below until the subject stands out cleanly. Click OK. Every selected bitmap changes in one undo step. Options Background TraceDraw learns the background's colors from the edges of the picture (up to four, so a gradient or a two-tone backdrop works). To choose them yourself, click the eyedropper and click the background in a preview; each click adds a color. Click a color swatch to take it out, and Automatic to go back to the learnt colors. Tolerance How far a color may be from the background's and still count as background (0 to 100). Raise it when some backdrop stays; lower it when parts of the subject go. Edge softness Feathers the edge of the subject, in pixels. 0 keeps a hard edge. Contiguous (on at first) Only the background connected to the edges of the picture goes, so a white shirt on a white backdrop keeps its inside. Turn it off to remove every pixel near a background color, for example the holes of a letter or a ring. Remove specks (on at first) Small loose spots left in the background go too. Clean edge colors (on at first) Takes the old background's color out of the half-transparent pixels of the edge, so no light or dark halo shows when the subject goes on another background. Reset puts every option back. Tips It works best on a backdrop that differs from the subject: a studio background, a sky, a product on a plain table. For busy scenes, the AI command Remove Background with AI (see AI) separates subject and scene by their meaning. The result replaces the pixels; effects on the bitmap are made permanent. To fine-tune afterwards, use Masking colors.

Afdrukken TraceDraw drukt af door een drukklare PDF van de vellen te maken, die de viewer van uw systeem naar de printer stuurt. Deze pagina's leggen het dialoogvenster Afdrukken en het voorbeeld uit, hoe u gegevens in een ontwerp samenvoegt om veel versies af te drukken, hoe u een tekening controleert voor het afdrukken en hoe u spandoeken afwerkt met een rand en zeilogen.

h: General Color Composite Layout Prepress PostScript and issues Print preview Other ways to print
x: Printing a drawing Choose File > Print (Ctrl+P). TraceDraw builds a PDF of the sheets and opens it in your system's viewer, where you choose the printer and print. In the browser version, the PDF is downloaded.  General Destination: the printer, a PDF file or a PostScript file. Orientation: match the layout, portrait or landscape. Print range: the whole document, the current page, a list of pages (such as 1-3, 5, 8-), or the selected objects. Copies, collated as whole sets or not. Print as bitmap: each sheet becomes one picture at the resolution you give. Color Composite prints all colors on each sheet; Separations prints one gray page per ink (cyan, magenta, yellow, black, then each spot ink). Convert spot colors to CMYK prints spot inks as their CMYK mix. Composite Print text in black. Always overprint black: full black fills and outlines print over the colors beneath. Layout As in document, Fit to page, or Scale to a percentage. Bleed limit: how far beyond the page objects print (4 mm at first). The imposition: several pages on one sheet, or a booklet, whose pages are paired for folding, with the sheet size and the gap between pages. A sketch shows the result. Prepress Invert and Mirror the whole sheet, for film. Print file information (the drawing's name or your own text, the page numbers, sheet number and date) and Print page numbers. Crop marks (and fold marks for booklets), Registration marks, Color bars and Densitometer scale. PostScript and issues With a PostScript file as the destination, the PostScript tab sets the language level (2 or 3). The Issues tab shows what the preflight check finds; see Preflight. Apply keeps the settings for the next time; see Global options for the defaults. Print preview File > Print Preview, or Print preview in the Print dialog box, shows the sheets exactly as they will print, with the imposition and the marks. The bar at the top has Print, Close, the sheet shown with previous and next (PgUp, PgDn), the plate to show while printing separations, and the zoom. The options on the left change the sheets at once. Other ways to print File > Send To saves a PDF to your desktop or documents folder, or attaches it to an email. Publish to PDF writes a PDF with full control of its settings; see Publishing to PDF.

h: Setting up a merge Kinds of field Editing the records
x: Print merge Print merge fills a design with data, to make many versions of it: name badges, numbered tickets, certificates, labels with QR codes. Each record of your data becomes a copy of the page, filled in. Setting up a merge Design the page. Where a value goes, type the field name in angle brackets in a text object, such as <Name>. Choose File > Print Merge > Create/Load Print Merge. Add the data: Import file reads a CSV file whose first line names the fields; or Add column to add fields by hand, then add records with +. Click Finish.  The current page is copied once per record, right after it, and each copy is filled in. The copies are named after the page and the record number. Kinds of field Text: replaces <Field> in every text of the page. Number: a counter you do not type: a start, a step and a number of digits (start 7, step 3, digits 3 gives 007, 010, 013). Picture: the cell holds the path of a picture. A text holding only <Field> becomes the picture, as large as fits its box. QR code: a text holding only <Field> becomes a QR code of the cell's text. An empty cell, or a picture that does not load, removes that object from the record's page. Editing the records Configure columns renames fields, changes their type and counter settings, and removes fields. View single record shows one record as a form; use the arrows or Go to record to move through them. The placeholder buttons insert a field into the text you are editing. Save data source writes the records as a CSV file. Edit Print Merge reopens the records, and Perform Merge runs the merge again.

h: The checks Using the list
x: Preflight Preflight checks a drawing for what tends to go wrong in print, before you print it or send it to a print shop. Choose File > Preflight. The Print dialog box also runs the checks and shows how many issues it found.  The checks Empty text object text with nothing in it Text does not fit its frame paragraph text with hidden lines Font not installed text in a font that is not installed Very small text text smaller than 5 points as printed Small text in rich black small black text made of several inks RGB color in a CMYK drawing screen colors in a drawing meant for print Object off the page objects outside the page and its bleed Low-resolution bitmap bitmaps below 200 dpi as placed Very high-resolution bitmap bitmaps above 1200 dpi Very thin outline outlines thinner than 0.1 mm White set to overprint white that would vanish when printed Empty page pages with no objects Objects that will not print objects on hidden or non-printing layers Warnings are likely problems; notes are worth a look. Using the list The top of the box shows the outcome. Each kind of issue has a heading with its count; click it to open or close it. Click an issue to go to its page and select its object. Under the list, the box says what to do about the kind you picked. Check again runs the checks again after you fix things. Choose checks turns checks on and off and sets their limits: the bitmap resolutions, the smallest text sizes and the thinnest outline. Defaults puts them back.

h: Source Border Grommets
x: Border and grommets Tools > Border and Grommet finishes large prints such as banners and canvases: it grows the page by a border and places grommet marks, where the eyelets will be punched, along its edge.  The preview on the left shows the final page, the border band, the original area (dashed) and the grommets, with the final height and width. Source Choose Page, or Selection to make the box of the selected objects the page. Border Tick Add border and choose its type: Mirror the edges: the design is mirrored out into the border; Stretch the edges: the edge pixels are stretched out; Solid color: the border is filled with one color. Set the size (31.75 mm at first), the same on every side. The design stays where it is; mirrored and stretched edges are made from a picture of the design, placed behind it, so your objects stay editable. Grommets Tick Add grommets, then set: Use border area: center each grommet in the border band; Size: the diameter of the grommet (6.35 mm at first); Margin: from the outer edge to the grommet (31.75 mm at first). Under Placement and distribution, choose the edges (corners, top, bottom, left, right; all at first), then the number of grommets per edge (4 at first) or the spacing between them. Corner grommets are shared by the two edges. The grommets are drawn as thin circles on a layer of their own. Reset puts every field back; OK is available when a border or grommets are on.

Webafbeeldingen Afbeeldingen voor webpagina's, apps en schermen zijn meestal bitmaps (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) op schermresolutie, of SVG-bestanden die op elk formaat scherp blijven. Deze pagina's leggen uit hoe u ze één voor één exporteert en hoe u veel pagina's en objecten tegelijk exporteert. Objecten kunnen ook koppelingen bevatten die werken in geëxporteerde SVG-, HTML- en PDF-bestanden; zie Koppelingen en bladwijzers.

h: Choosing a format Size and resolution Before exporting text
x: Exporting for the web File > Export For > Web opens the Export dialog box set up for screens: PNG at 96 dpi. It keeps its own settings, apart from Export. Office does the same for office documents (PNG at 150 dpi).  Choosing a format PNG: sharp edges and transparency; best for logos, icons and illustrations. JPEG: small files for photos; no transparency. Set the quality (1 to 100). WebP: small files with transparency; set the quality. GIF: few colors, with transparency. SVG: vector graphics that stay sharp at any size and keep links and object names. HTML: a web page with the drawing. Size and resolution For bitmap formats, set the resolution, or type the width or height in pixels: the other side follows the proportions of the page. For a 32 by 32 pixel icon, type 32. With Transparent background on, the empty parts of the page stay transparent in PNG, WebP and GIF files. Selected only exports only the selected objects, cropped to them; All pages exports every page. The preview shows what will be written, and the dialog box estimates the file size. Before exporting text Text > Make Text Web-compatible simplifies text for the web. To export many pages or objects at once, see The Export panel.

h: Adding assets Exporting
x: The Export panel The Export panel keeps a list of assets (pages and objects) and exports them all at once, each in its own format, to one folder: the icons of an app in several sizes, every page of a set of social media posts. Open it from Window > Panels.  Adding assets Add pages adds every page of the drawing, named after the page. Add selection adds the selected objects as one asset, cropped to them, named after the object. New assets take the format and resolution set under New assets (PNG at 150 dpi at first). Each asset has a tick (only ticked assets are exported), its name (the file name), its format, its resolution for bitmap formats (72 to 2400 dpi) and a cross to remove it. The link under the name goes to the page or selects the objects. Exporting Click Browse to choose the folder (the first export asks for one). Click Export. The button shows how many assets will be written. Characters that files cannot have in their name become _, and two assets with the same name get " (2)", " (3)" and so on. The status bar says how many files were written. In the browser, every file is downloaded.

Bestandsindelingen TraceDraw slaat op in zijn eigen indeling, .tdraw, die alles bewaart, en slaat ook .cdr-bestanden op. Het opent en importeert veel andere indelingen en exporteert vector-, bitmap- en drukindelingen. Deze pagina's noemen de indelingen en leggen importeren, exporteren en publiceren naar PDF uit.
